title: The Empirical Variability of Narrative Perceptions of Social Media Texts

live_model.evidence: Footnote 9: "GPT-4-Turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)"; Table 2 row "researcher / GPT-4t 0.379 28% behavior_strategy -0.11 1% - -" (Cohen's kappa vs. researcher labels)

prompt.location: Appendix E ("LLM Prompts"), full JSON-output template printed with 5 question paraphrases
prompt.note: Majority vote over 5 paraphrased-prompt predictions per text forms the model's final label.

claim.metric: Cohen's kappa, GPT-4-Turbo descriptive story-labels vs. researcher (prescriptive) labels

data.source: Authors' social-media survey corpus; paper states "dataset of labels and texts (without any identifiers) will be released"; code at github.com/joel-mire/...

notes: EMNLP 2024 paper studying whether descriptive (crowd/LLM) vs. prescriptive (researcher) annotations agree on whether a social-media post "contains a story"; GPT-4-Turbo's label agreement is a direct object of study (like GPT-4, GPT-4o and Llama3 in the same table). Soft gap: the exact number of texts underlying the Table 2 kappa values is not stated in the excerpts read (N=886 appears only for a separate "rationales" analysis).
